title: Tiny offline SDK bootpack: size, memory & debug notebook
content:
Purpose:
A compact working notebook for the tiny/offline mobile SDK bootpack: concrete size and mem budgets, quickstart steps for building a hermetic demo, and a terse debug checklist for first-10-minutes failures. This is a working riff (notes-to-self + eng experiments) — not final API copy.

TL;DR (Two-line):
- Target: <6MB added to app binary (AAR + native libs) for a minimal offline inference client with lightweight tokenization and a 1–2MB quantized model shard.
- Priority wins: aggressive symbol stripping, split native library flavors, lazy init + background warmup, and a simple smoke test runner for CI.

Personas:
- Mobile eng integrating SDK for offline assistant/embedding use-cases (Android + iOS).
- SDK eng working on packaging/stripping pipelines.
- Field SEs building hermetic demos for constrained devices.

Goals (short-term):
- Define a reproducible APK/AAB size budget and a CI size gate.
- Create a 10-minute quickstart: stub server mode -> hermetic local mode with prepackaged assets.
- Telemetry minimal: boot time, peak RSS, first-response latency, bundle checksum.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Added app binary size <= 6MB (baseline app + tiny-SDK).
- Cold-start to first token <= 350ms on mid-tier device (Android 2019-ish).
- CI flakiness < 0.5% for smoke-runner across matrixed ABI.

Size & memory budget (initial proposal):
- Java/Kotlin wrapper + resources: 0.6 MB
- Native library (strip, -Os, split by arch): target 2.2 MB per arch (arm64-v8a flavor primary).
- Model shard (int8/4-bit): 1.5 MB (quantized tiny embed model / distilled LM micro-shard)
- Tokenizer assets: 0.15 MB (merged vocab + small BPE map)
- Telemetry shim + config: 0.2 MB
- Safety margin + packaging overhead: 0.35 MB
= Total ~5.2 MB (target round to 6MB)
Memory (runtime):
- Heap budget (app-visible): <20 MB additional at steady state (includes token buffers + request queue).
- Native RSS peak allowed: <40 MB on 2GB devices.

Packaging decisions and heuristics:
- Use split APK/AAB to push non-critical arch binaries to a separate split (keeps base install smaller).
- Provide a dynamic-download model path for optional larger variants; enforce retry/backoff.
- Prefer single small quantized shard vs full model; server-side scoring for heavier tasks.
- Use LTO and strip-unneeded symbols. Build variants: tiny, tiny+debug, full (for internal apps).

Initialization flow (recommended minimal):
1) App creates SDKClient with options {lazyInit: true, modelPathStrategy: "bundled-or-dl", telemetry: minimal}
2) SDK returns fast handle synchronously (<5ms) with no heavy native calls.
3) Background thread performs native library load + mmap of model shard; emits "model_mapped" event.
4) First inference path uses pre-allocated token buffer; if model not ready, fallback to queued no-op response with code 202 (warming).

Quickstart (10-min demo sequence):
- Pre-reqs: Android Studio, gradle wrapper, sample-app repo branch tiny-bootpack-experiment.
- Steps:
  a) checkout branch and run ./gradlew :app:assembleTinyDemo
  b) install split/dynamic feature if using AAB: adb install-multiple base.apk splits/arm64_v8a.apk
  c) Launch app -> Settings -> Enable 'Hermetic Local' -> Tap 'Warm'. App logs should show: SDK:init_fast_handle, native_load_start, model_mapped, ready.
  d) Run sample prompt -> observed first-token latency printed in UI.

Smoke tests for CI (must be quick):
- build tiny artifact (all ABIs) -> run emulator device matrix (arm64 only if resource limited).
- Run 'smoke-runner --scenario basic-completion --max-time 1s' -> pass if first-token < 350ms.
- Size gate check: unzip AAR or APK and assert compressed sizes for target files.

Developer ergonomics & UX notes:
- Keep Java API surface tiny: SDKClient.create(context, options) and client.request(prompt)->TokenStream.
- Provide a debug overlay to show current model path, checksum, and last telemetry ping. Keep togglable via long-press.
- Error codes: define compact set for offline mode: OFFLINE_OK, OFFLINE_WARMING, OFFLINE_MISSING_MODEL, OFFLINE_BAD_CHECKSUM, OFFLINE_RESOURCE_LIMIT.

Debug checklist (first-10-minutes):
- If app never emits native_load_start: verify library packaging in APK (use ./gradlew :app:installDebug && readelf).
- If model_mapped missing: check file path inside assets vs merged resources; confirm model shard extracted to app cache path.
- If first-token high: attach simple perf trace (Android systrace) and inspect mmap faults.
- If CI fails intermittently: ensure emulator cold boot vs snapshot differences; prefer cold boot for size gate runs.

Prompts & edge-case experiments to capture:
- Multi-request burst while warming -> does KV cache allocate excessive memory? (observed ~12MB transient in early tests)
- Interrupted download + resume: ensure partial files cleaned and retry.
- Low-storage device: verify graceful degrade and clear user-facing message.

Telemetry plan (minimal & privacy mindful):
- Send only anonymized metrics: boot_latency_ms, model_sha_short, checksum_ok (y/n), arch, event (model_mapped, native_load).
- Batch & upload on network available; allow opt-out. No user prompt content should be recorded.

Known open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default shard quantization format and produce reference script (PR2 in repo).
- Determine whether to include a tiny tokenizer written in pure Kotlin to avoid native BPE for smallest installs.
- Validate memory budgets across a matrix of old devices (Moto G5, Pixel 2, iPhone SE 1st gen).
- Create CI size gate artifact extractor script (TODO: write acceptance tests, assign to Ethan).

Quick hacks (notes-to-self):
- Try compressing model shard with zstd+mmap and use streaming decompressor to reduce on-disk size but keep in-memory footprint predictable.
- Prototype a 'bootstrapper' tiny lib that defers most native symbols until warm path called to reduce initial linking time.

Links & references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-mobile/pull/218
- Jira: JIRA-DEVEXP-712 (tiny-bootpack workstream)
- Internal notes: CONFLUENCE-ENG-4892 (packaging experiments)

Appendix: rough experiment log
- 2024-10-22: first alpine-based cross-compile produced 3.8MB arm64 library (no strip).
- 2024-11-01: enabling -s symbol strip + LTO shrank to 2.3MB (good).
- 2024-12-12: int8 quantization script produced 1.4MB shard but increased latency on small inputs (trade-off).

End of notebook — rough, intentionally terse. Next steps: turn this into a reproducible checklist and add a CI pipeline job that runs size-check + smoke-runner.

Notes-to-self: if we want to pitch tiny offline to partners, prepare a one-pager with install-time tradeoffs and recommended fallback UX.
